title: Diwali 2026 Falls on Sunday, November 8: The Five-Day Calendar for US and India
excerpt: Lakshmi Puja is Sunday, November 8 everywhere, but the surrounding days shift by location: the US runs Dhanteras November 6 to Bhai Dooj November 10, while India's Govardhan Puja and Bhai Dooj fall a day later.
body:
• Diwali (Lakshmi Puja) falls on Sunday, November 8, 2026, in both India and the United States — the main evening is agreed by every calendar checked.
  • In the US, the five days run Friday November 6 (Dhanteras) through Tuesday November 10 (Bhai Dooj), per Drik Panchang dates for US cities.
  • Relatives in India follow a shifted tail: Govardhan Puja is Tuesday November 10 and Bhai Dooj Wednesday November 11 there — neither side is wrong; the tithi lands differently by location.
  • US Lakshmi Puja muhurat on November 8: 5:03–6:52 PM in New York, 4:54–6:41 PM in Chicago, 5:51–7:46 PM in Houston and 5:21–7:12 PM in the Bay Area — plan leave, school and travel around your own city's dates.

Diwali 2026 falls on Sunday, November 8 — a date every major calendar agrees on, from Drik Panchang's New Delhi, New York and Los Angeles calendars to the Hindu American Foundation's holiday guide. The complication is the four days around it. Because each festival day is assigned by the lunar tithi in force at a set local time, the five-day sequence runs differently in the United States than in India, and families coordinating calls, leave and travel across both need the right set for the city they are actually in.

The five days in the United States

For US families, the Diwali 2026 USA guide, using Drik Panchang dates, lists Dhanteras on Friday, November 6; Naraka Chaturdashi (Choti Diwali) on Saturday, November 7; Diwali and Lakshmi Puja on Sunday, November 8; Govardhan Puja and Annakut on Monday, November 9; and Bhai Dooj on Tuesday, November 10. Amavasya runs from 12:57 AM on November 8 to 2:01 AM on November 9, New York time, so the new-moon evening covers Diwali night in every US time zone.

The Sunday main day is a genuine break for American families: the biggest evening of the year does not compete with a working day. The pressure moves to the edges instead — Dhanteras is a Friday, and Govardhan Puja and Bhai Dooj fall on a Monday and Tuesday, which is when school-absence requests and early finishes at work need to be arranged.

Why India runs a day later at the tail

In India, the same calendars put Naraka Chaturdashi on the morning of Sunday, November 8 itself, Govardhan Puja on Tuesday, November 10, and Bhai Dooj on Wednesday, November 11. As the Ghar family planner explains, neither set is wrong: a tithi begins at one instant worldwide, but that instant falls at a different local time in each place, so an observance can land on a different calendar date in North America than in India. The practical rule is to use the dates for your own city, not a relative's forwarded screenshot — and to write both sets, labelled by city, into a shared family calendar if relatives abroad are working to different days. Regional observances add their own lines: Tamil Deepavali falls on November 7 in the US calendars, and Gujarati New Year on November 9.

Lakshmi Puja timings, city by city

Lakshmi Puja is performed on Amavasya evening during Pradosh Kaal, the roughly two and a half hours after sunset, with the published muhurat marking the portion when the fixed Vrishabha lagna is rising. On Sunday, November 8, the muhurat is 5:03 to 6:52 PM in New York, 4:54 to 6:41 PM in Chicago, 5:51 to 7:46 PM in Houston and 5:21 to 7:12 PM in the Bay Area, all local time. US daylight saving time ends on Sunday, November 1, a week before Diwali, so every one of those times is standard time — and puja will start about an hour earlier on the clock than families used to October temple programmes may expect. Never convert India's muhurat to US time; converted timings land in the American early morning. Use a panchang calculated for your own city.

Planning the fortnight

Public celebrations cluster on the weekends either side: Diwali at Times Square runs on Saturday, October 24 — see our coverage of Diwali at Times Square's 11th edition — with Seattle's Lights of India on November 7 and Houston's festival at Discovery Green on November 14. Temples typically publish their own Diwali schedules only a few weeks ahead, and a temple programme is often set by a hall booking or a weekend rather than the tithi calculation, so confirm your congregation's actual evening separately.

For travel, the shape of the week matters more than any single date: anyone flying to India for the festival should decide which days the trip is really for — the US sequence ends November 10, India's on November 11 — and book around those, since festival-season fares rise through October. Gifts and sweets crossing borders should already be moving; pair anything posted internationally with a local fallback in case it arrives late.
